items.title: "We got this wrong… We do not support AI-generated music": D'Addario admits generative AI was used on string demo video after all
items.excerpt: D'Addario reversed its denial and confirmed Suno Studio was used to "regenerate the original track" in its NYXL HD electric guitar string demo video. The brand apologised for sharing inaccurate information and for deleting critical comments, and says its process will change going forward.

items.title: Suno announces vinyl pressing service for AI-generated music
items.excerpt: Suno users can now compile tracks from their library into a custom 12-inch record holding up to 46 minutes of audio, pressed and shipped by Suno for around $45 plus shipping. It pushes prompt-generated music into a physical, collectible format for the first time.

items.title: We can't outrun AI, but we can stop tripping over ourselves
items.excerpt: With AI uploads flooding streaming services, the argument is that the industry's edge is human connection, not output speed. The practical takeaway: stop racing generative volume and instead strip out the administrative friction that slows real artists down.

items.title: "We have a clear set of principles rooted in supporting artistry and creativity", says Suno CEO after latest legal defeat
items.excerpt: After the German court ruling, Suno's CEO says the platform will add audio watermarking and limit downloads to curb AI slop and fraud. The company still declined to disclose its training data sources or how rights holders would be compensated.

items.title: NAM A2 Pedals & Software: This gear supports Neural Amp Modeler A2 in 2026
items.excerpt: Neural Amp Modeler's Architecture 2 standard runs 30–40% more efficiently than A1 while sounding better, packing full and lite neural captures into a single file that hardware picks automatically. Headrush, Mooer, Hotone and Nux shipped firmware support within weeks.

items.title: Push Hack, very unauthorized access to Push 3's display, files, MIDI, and more
items.excerpt: Federico Pepe's Push Hack opens SSH access to Ableton Push 3's Linux layer, giving full control of the display, file system and MIDI routing. Notably, it was built with AI-assisted coding agents — a reminder that machine learning is now very good at reverse-engineering closed music hardware.

items.title: OMNi (alpha v0.1), a FREE Rust-based DAW with native AI sample generation
items.excerpt: Developer Tomasz Głuc has released OMNi, a free DAW written entirely in Rust with AI sample generation and image-to-sound synthesis built into the core rather than bolted on as a plugin. It's an early alpha, but it points at what a natively generative DAW looks like.

items.title: The era of unlabeled AI content in Europe is ending
items.excerpt: From August 2, the EU AI Act requires AI-generated or AI-manipulated audio, images, video and text to be clearly marked as artificial. It leans on disclosure and training-data documentation rather than restriction, leaving copyright fights to the courts.

items.title: German court says Suno's AI training infringed copyright in landmark ruling
items.excerpt: The Munich Regional Court found Suno unlawfully trained on protected compositions from GEMA's repertoire without authorisation. The ruling establishes that training conducted in the US does not shield an AI company from copyright liability in Europe.

items.title: Quiet Riot, Ozzy bassist Rudy Sarzo on how he uses AI
items.excerpt: Veteran bassist Rudy Sarzo describes using Suno as a working studio band to finish songs on his own. His framing is practical rather than ideological: AI removes the studio-time and label gatekeeping that used to decide which ideas ever got recorded.

items.title: Sonarworks expand SoundID VoiceAI library
items.excerpt: Sonarworks added a C-Pop Voices Expansion Pack of 10 Chinese voice models to SoundID VoiceAI, aimed at Mandopop and Cantopop production. The models were trained on ethically sourced material with artist consent and compensation.

items.title: Songwriter AI victory in Europe as GEMA beats Suno in copyright lawsuit
items.excerpt: A German court ruled Suno infringed copyright by training on GEMA-controlled compositions without permission. The decision requires Suno to stop using the entire GEMA repertoire unless it secures proper licensing.
